riemtorch

RIEMANNIAN OPTIMIZATION IN R

Your objective. Its geometry.
One torch workflow.

Optimize user-defined tensor objectives on spheres, matrix manifolds, hyperbolic spaces, and products. Use automatic differentiation, choose a solver, and run on a compatible CPU or GPU.

Get started Explore examples

A first optimization

Find the unit vector most aligned with a target. The sphere supplies the geometry; the objective is an ordinary scalar torch expression.

library(torch)
library(riemtorch)

M <- manifold.sphere(3)
target <- torch_tensor(c(1, 2, 3), dtype = torch_float64())
x0 <- torch_tensor(c(1, 0, 0), dtype = torch_float64())
problem <- riem.problem(
  M, function(x, data) -torch_sum(x * data), data = target
)

fit <- riem.optimize(problem, x0, method = "conjugate_gradient")
fit$point  # approximately c(0.2673, 0.5345, 0.8018)
fit$termination

The run selects a compatible device automatically. Add device = "cpu" to force CPU execution, including on a CUDA workstation. Registered data moves with the problem. Learn about devices and precision.

Learn with public data

Explore ten worked examples in the example gallery, from short introductions to complete applications. Every example includes executable code, figures, and numerical checks.

Penguin measurementsFind a two-dimensional subspace and compare deterministic and finite-sum optimization. Industrial measurementsCompare quadratic and Huber regression on observations from an ammonia plant. Missing air-quality readingsFit a compact low-rank matrix and evaluate predictions on held-out observations. Covariance geometryAverage covariance matrices from observed time series using two geometric metrics. Tree-volume constraintsEncode nonnegative scaling exponents and check the constrained optimum. Sparse car-data regressionWrite an exact proximal operator and trace coefficients across penalty strengths.

The data are built into R or bundled locally with attribution. See data sources and reproducibility for citations, preprocessing, and downloads.

Installation

Install the package from GitHub and set up the R torch runtime:

install.packages(c("remotes", "torch"))
if (!torch::torch_is_installed()) torch::install_torch()
remotes::install_github("kisungyou/riemtorch")

To install a local checkout instead, open riemtorch.Rproj and use Build → Install Package in RStudio.

riemtorch uses R torch as its numerical backend and contains no compiled extension of its own. The getting-started guide walks through installation, your first solve, and interpretation of the result.

Know what is supported

riem.capabilities(M) describes the operations supported by a geometry. riem.support() exposes the evidence tables. Solver convergence, derivative support, and hardware qualification are separate questions; consult numerical limitations when selecting a method.

Manifold means and PCA here are worked optimization examples. For a collection of statistical methods on manifolds, see the author’s Riemann package.

Build this documentation locally

With riemtorch.Rproj open in RStudio:

install.packages("pkgdown")  # only needed once
pkgdown::build_site()

The site is written to docs/ and opens in your browser in an interactive session. You can also open docs/index.html directly. No deployment is needed.
